result.reason: H1 persists a compact semantic checkpoint for session resumption. The training evidence shows a consistent regularity: externalizing identity/state/commitments becomes durable capital only when the stored subset is not recoverable from any other owner's truth AND there is an independent owner-respecting consumer. T2 (task-continuity) demonstrates TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL precisely because private commitments and unknown external effects survive replacement with a clear owner and lifecycle, exactly the 'smaller subset... unavailable anywhere else' clause in H1. But H1 explicitly has a larger reconstructable portion that duplicates current owner truth, which duplicates truth (like T6's global writable usage db, NO_CAPITAL) and re-invokes the pro-graph/anti-graph tension of T3 (NO_CAPITAL: simpler current-source retrieval baselines never failed, no independent consumer requires graph authority). The unrecoverable subset gives real but bounded option-value analogous to T5's opaque immutable binding + digest (SCOPED_CAPITAL: one real non-Evaluation owner composition did not yet demonstrate a shared schema) and T4's run-once read-only exporter with rebuildable projection (owner recovery independent of projection). The checkpoint is useful at a bounded/local resume scope via a read-only projection that does not supersede owner truth, but there is no demonstrated independent consumer whose responsibility requires a promoted shared semantic boundary (T8), so it is not demonstrated TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. Net: useful within a bounded, owner-local read-only scope — SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H1 proposes a compact cross-session checkpoint so future Agents can resume without rereading full history. The visible evidence supports only a bounded/partial value: the reconstructable subset of the checkpoint duplicates current owner truth (T4/T6 show the value of read-only projections is bounded and should never become a new writable authority), so its distinct value comes only from a smaller subset containing participant-selected commitments and unresolved identities that are not otherwise recoverable. That unrecoverable-subset behavior parallels T2 (durable owner state with clear lifecycle), but H1 is framed as a generic 'compact checkpoint across sessions,' not a stable owner-owned durable state with a demonstrated independent consumer. The transcript/session-only baseline failure in T2 was specific to private commitments and unknown external effects; H1 is a generalization that does not yet show a materially independent consumer consuming the checkpoint's relation semantics repeatedly (as in T4), nor repeated owner-controlled promotion (as in T7/T8). Unlike T1/T3/T5 where a shared kernel, graph authority, or shared schema was unpromoted or NO_CAPITAL, H1 is not reconstructing a working mechanism and is not a new global writable authority, so it is not clearly NO_CAPITAL. But the evidence shows no demonstrated broad, stable, independent consumption, so TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is not supported either. The checkpoint is useful only at a local/option-value scope: it cheaply restores an Agent's context where the reconstructable fraction is redundant and only a smaller commitment/identity fraction carries real recovery value, and that value has not been shown at a broad transferable scope.

H2 keeps digest-bound scoped HTTPS CONNECT paths as a secondary, bounded option-value mechanism alongside ambient networking that already satisfies all tested useful work. The evidence pattern that predicts SCOPED_CAPITAL is T5/O3: maintaining an opaque binding/option that has not yet demonstrated a shared or standard use by independent consumers, yet remains retained for a bounded scope. Like T5's digest-comparable immutable binding, the scoped paths have a plausible future reward (faster services, fallback under ambient failure) but no independent consumer demonstrates broad transferable value now. They also demand dedicated services and qualification, matching the 'own the mechanics already exist (ambient networking) and a new surface becomes extra authority/compatibility cost' warnings from T1/T3/T6 that caution against promotion. The change is retained and consumed at a local/partial scope rather than deleted (not NO_CAPITAL), but there is no repeated independent responsibility or unowned stable semantic boundary yet to lift it to TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. So the prediction is SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H2 retains an optional, digest-bound scoped egress mechanism beside ambient networking. The evidence shows the scoped paths are not yet needed for any completed work (ambient already completes all tested useful work) and offer only potential option value, speed on some services, or resilience under hypothetical future ambient failures. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern in the training evidence: changes that are useful at a bounded/local/partial/option-value scope but are not demonstrated as broad transferable capital. By contrast, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL in the training set consistently involves later independent consumption or repeated cross-owner responsibility (e.g., T4's read-only exporters consumed by formal evaluation, T7's method consumed by self-audit, T6/T1 owner-native projections), which H2 lacks — there is no independent consumer or demonstrated repeated responsibility for the scoped paths. NO_CAPITAL would apply if the change were failed or rejected outright, but H2 is retained, not deleted/promoted as broadly reusable, so the bounded option-value framing (SCOPED) is the best-supported prediction. The dual existence of ambient as a fallback and the unproven shared benefit keep it scoped rather than transferred.

H3 (game-responsibility-prior) is a model-visible responsibility/feedback prior carried from one bounded domain (Game work) into a later related domain (rescue behavior). It changes how the model reasons about custody and responsibility, which is a real reusable reasoning prior rather than a frozen product promotion — but its later effect is explicitly indirect and depends on many subsequent policy choices, so no independent consumer demonstrates broad transferable authority. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern: useful at a bounded/local/option-value scope (a reasoning prior within the owner's own decision procedure) without evidence of a stable, independently-consumed shared semantic boundary. It is not NO_CAPITAL because the prior has demonstrated retained reusable value across a later task attempt, and not TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because the reliance is indirect and mediated by later choices rather than repeated unowned independent consumption (contrast T7, where the preserved method was consumed both by the experiment loop and by Computer self-audit under a frozen oracle/authority boundary).

H3 (game-responsibility-prior) is a model-visible prior that changes how the model reasons about custody and responsibility, and it is applied to later rescue behavior. The evidence for later value is indirect and contingent on many subsequent policy choices, exactly the kind of bounded/partial/option-value scope that maps to SCOPED_CAPITAL rather than TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL in the training evidence requires later independent consumption by a materially independent consumer or repeated responsibility at a stable evidenced scope (e.g., T4/T6 projection consuming the same relation semantics under a real owner, T7 consumed later by Computer self-audit, or T8 guiding heterogeneous later decisions as a reusable rule). H3's prior is neither demonstrated as independently consumed by a separate owner nor as a repeatable rule; it only weakly shapes one agent's later reasoning, so NO_CAPITAL is too weak (it is retained and has some adaptive use) and TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is too strong. This places it in the SCOPED_CAPITAL bucket, the middle category for usefulness at a bounded/local/partial scope without demonstrated broad transferable value.

The holdout H4 moves exact repeated source-history aggregation into a deterministic Security-local reducer/projection, exactly matching the pattern evidenced in T4 (run-once read-only owner exporters plus rebuildable projection, consumed by multiple owners) and T7's bounded method with clear authority boundary and falsifier. However, T4 was TRANSFERRED while T5 (similar binding/composition idea) was SCOPED because the second real non-Evaluation consumer had not yet demonstrated a shared schema, and T6 shows owner-native read-only projection does NOT justify a global writable/shared authority. H4 is a single-owner (Security-local), precision-sensitive, exact-escape-hatch projection where the model must still interpret correctly, i.e., a bounded/local/option-value mechanism rather than a demonstrated broad transferable authority. There is no visible evidence of a second independent owner consuming the same projection semantics, so transfer has not been demonstrated. The residue of uncertainty (model interpretation dependency) further keeps it at option-value scope. I predict SCOPED_CAPITAL: useful at a bounded, owner-local, option-value scope, but not yet demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H4 externalizes a precision-sensitive, owner-scoped reduction (source-history aggregation) into a deterministic Security-local projection, which is later consumed but the model still must interpret the projection. This matches the T4 pattern: an owner-local, run-once read-only projection/query that reconstructs trajectories without becoming shared authority, consumed by multiple owners/evaluation while recovery stays independent. T4 is labeled SCOPED_CAPITAL (observed outcome 3), and I infer that mapping from the parallel structural evidence. Unlike T2 (durable owner state lifecycle, TRANSFERRED) or T6/T8 (global writable authority/shared boundary, NO/SCOPED), H4 does not establish a new cross-owner authority and is bounded to a Security-local mechanism with an exact escape hatch, so it demonstrates reusable value only at a local/option-value scope, not broad transfer. The 'exact escape hatch' and 'model must still interpret' language also signals deferred/partial automation, consistent with SCOPED rather than TRANSFERRED.

The holdout change H5 encodes a production rule scoped to expression/layout correctness (render-review-prior). Its value is a bounded, well-defined procedure with a direct observable artifact (rendered pixels), a bounded correction path, and exact unchanged controls, and it is intended for later ordinary Web/Studio production rather than one page. This resembles T4/T5/T7 patterns where a small, owner-local, rebuildable procedure is reused, but crucially the evidence shows reuse remains within a bounded/local scope rather than becoming a broad authority. General-purpose mechanisms (mature layout/browser systems) already own much of the underlying mechanics, and the rule inherits rather than replaces them, matching T8's 'smallest owner-local projection first' guidance and the promotion only after repeated unowned stable responsibility. The outcome is genuine but bounded reusable value (multiple later Web/Studio pages in the same semantic domain), with no evidence of independent, cross-domain, or transferred responsibility requiring a shared authority. This maps most cleanly to SCOPED_CAPITAL (useful at a bounded/local/option-value scope, not demonstrated as broad transferable capital), and is consistent with the observed outcome multiset containing exactly one SCOPED_CAPITAL (outcome 3) already assignable to a bounded-projection change plus this rule as the second SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H5 is a retained production rule with a direct observable artifact, bounded correction path, and exact unchanged controls, intended for later ordinary Web/Studio production. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL profile: useful at a bounded/local scope (Web/Studio rendering review) without demonstrated broad transfer as a generalized shared semantic boundary or authority. Mapping the multiset to T1-T8: TRANSFERRED items correspond to T2, T4, T7 and one more (T4/T7 clearly transfer as repeatedly consumed; T2 durable owner state), NO_CAPITAL to T1 and T3 (kernel and graph not promoted as general changes), leaving SCOPED_CAPITAL for T5 and T8. T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule) is a reusable decision rule intended to guide heterogeneous decisions but is only demonstrated at a rule/value scope, not as a consumed shared boundary, so it is SCOPED not TRANSFERRED. By analogy, H5's rule is similarly bounded to a specific domain (pixel-level rendering verification) and specific artifact class; it has a direct artifact and correction path but no evidence of independent cross-owner consumption or repeated responsibility beyond its intended production domain. Therefore SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H6 matches the pattern of owner-local read-only projections that survive because they eliminate repeated manual reconstruction cost without becoming a new writable authority. Like T4 (read-only owner exporters plus rebuildable projection, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) it externalizes only a narrow read-only projection; but unlike T4, H6 has a single owner (Agents repeatedly reconstructing route affordances) and no demonstrated second independent consumer consuming the same relation semantics, nor a formal evaluation loop. It also avoids the failure modes of T3/T6 (which proposed writable shared authority/duplicate truth and were not promoted). The repeated reconstruction burden is confined to a bounded local scope (route affordances for the Workstation), native evidence stays reachable, and no central registry or writable authority is created. This predicts usefulness at a bounded/local scope in the Computing research context but not yet demonstrated broad transferrable capital, hence SCOPED_CAPITAL rather than TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL.

H6 is a narrow read-only projection (network capability/currentness) exposed to avoid Agents repeatedly reconstructing route affordances from raw configuration. It leaves route selection and all effects to the Agent, keeps native evidence reachable, and avoids a central capability registry. This mirrors the strongest evidenced pattern: T4 (run-once read-only owner exporters plus rebuildable projection) achieved TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because multiple owners and formal evaluation consumed the same relation semantics while recovery stayed independent of the projection, and T6's read-only projection of owner-native measurements was viable. But H6 is narrower and bounded to a single-owner, single-domain convenience surface (Workstation network affordances); no evidence shows a second independent consumer or repeated responsibility beyond the local Agents who currently reconstruct routes. This is exactly a bounded/local/option-value scope, not demonstrated as broad transferable capital, and it is not a failed/deleted change (it is useful at that local scope). Hence SCOPED_CAPITAL, not TRANSFERRED (no independent later consumer or repeated unowned responsibility demonstrated) and not NO_CAPITAL (it has demonstrable local reusable value by removing repeated reconstruction cost).

H7 carries T8's Infrastructure Promotion Rule forward as a fixed prompt prior. The training evidence maps T8 to observed outcome 8's label pattern: T8 is an intended-to-guide rule whose value depends on later heterogeneous decisions actually reusing it, but it is a soft constraint rather than a demonstrated independent consumer with stable unowned responsibility. The rule inherits mature mechanisms first and promotes shared boundaries only after repeated unowned stable responsibility, so as a prompt prior it adds no new owner facts and merely biases decisions. This is useful reinforcement/option value within a bounded scope (guiding architecture decisions inside Computing), not a repeated independent external consumption that would demonstrate TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, and not a failed side branch that would be NO_CAPITAL. The strongest evidence-supported analog is SCOPED_CAPITAL: bounded, local, option-value usefulness without demonstrated broad transfer, matching T8→outcome 8 in the unattributed multiset.

The holdout carries the Infrastructure Promotion Rule (T8) as a fixed prompt prior. The evidence for T8 itself is SCOPED_CAPITAL: the rule is a reusable guidance principle but explicitly 'intended to guide' and its promotion applies only 'after repeated unowned stable responsibility', with repository/service extraction gated separately — no repeated unowned stable responsibility is yet evidenced, so no broad transfer is demonstrated. The holdout merely re-routes the same textual rule into a new (heterogeneous architecture/owner) deployment as a fixed prior; it adds no new owner facts, and the change itself even flags that it 'may bias different model families differently' and its value is conditional on 'if the historical rule generalizes.' There is no independent consumer or repeated responsibility showing the compact prior transfers cleanly across owners; the value is bounded/conditional and option-valued, i.e. useful only within a local/potential scope rather than demonstrated as broad reusable capital. This is below TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL but above pure failure, matching SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H8 is a reusable procedure (a checklist asking about consumer, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, reopen/deletion) analogous to T7 and T8. In the evidence, the two items that encode a generalized, reusable decision rule or method rather than a specific mechanism are exactly the ones whose pattern maps to high-value labels. T7 (agent-first-research-method, a bounded procedure consumed by both the experiment loop and later Computer self-audit) and T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule, intended to guide heterogeneous later decisions) are decision procedures with later independent consumption, consistent with TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. The observed outcome multiset contains exactly four TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL labels, and T2, T4, T6, T7 are the strongest evidenced transfers (durable owner state, read-only projection consumed by multiple owners, owner-native projection, and the research method). A generic evidence-calibration procedure applied even to a materially different decision family is a rule with repeated independent consumption exactly like T8, so TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is the best-supported prediction. SCOPED_CAPITAL would understate it because the checklist is explicitly designed to transfer across heterogeneous decision families, not merely solve one bounded scope. NO_CAPITAL is unsupported because no evidence shows the checklist failed or was deleted.

The training evidence shows that reusable rules/procedures that generalize across heterogeneous decisions—rather than shared mechanisms or authorities—are the consistent winners. Specifically, T7 (agent-first-research-method, a bounded reusable method) was transferred, and T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule, a reusable decision rule intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions) also transferred. H8 shares this exact shape: it is a general evidence-calibration procedure, not a shared kernel/database/schema/graph (T1, T3, T6 all fell to NO_CAPITAL or SCOPED because they create new authority/compatibility or storage surfaces and duplicate existing mechanics). H8 encodes the decision discipline (ask current consumer, incremental outcome, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, reopen/deletion) and is applied to a materially different professional-equipment decision family, demonstrating independent transfer across domains analogous to T7/T8. There is no evidence that the checklist becomes a new writable authority or shared storage surface, so no NO_CAPITAL factor applies.
